nodes.name: Thermal CVD VGS growth on CF
nodes.procedure: The CF/VGSs were prepared by growing vertical graphene sheets on carbon felt in a tube furnace at 1200°C from the mixture of CH4 and H2, where the flow rates of CH4 and H2 are 6 and 160 sccm, respectively. As demonstrated in our previous paper, the CF/VGSs can be produced in large scale easily by thermal CVD.

nodes.name: Thermal CVD MoS2 growth on CF/VGSs
nodes.procedure: MoCl5 (99.99%, anhydrous, Sigma-Aldrich) and sulfur (99.99%, Sigma-Aldrich) were used as the precursors to prepare the MoS2 nanosheets. 30 mg of MoCl5, 0.15 g of sulfur powder, and CF/VGSs were placed in different crucibles... tube furnace was heated to 500°C under Ar atmosphere with a flow rate of 50 sccm. The heating rate is 20°C/min and the reaction time is 10 min.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition FeCoNi(OH)x
nodes.procedure: The FeCoNi(OH)x nanosheets were electrodeposited on MoS2 nanosheets in a standard three-electrode electrochemical system, where the CF/VGSs/MoS2, Pt foil, and Ag/AgCl were used as the working, counter, and reference electrode, respectively. The aqueous solution with 0.1 M Ni(NO3)2, 0.1 M Co(NO3)2, and 0.05 M Fe(NO3)3 was used as the electrodepositing solution. The electrodeposition was carried out for 200 s at a constant cathode voltage of -1.0 V. After electrodeposition, the obtained composite electrode was washed several times with deionized water and ethanol, and dried at 70°C in the air.

nodes.name: Phosphating conversion
nodes.procedure: The CF/VMFP were prepared by converting the FeCoNi(OH)x nanosheets into NiCoFePx nanosheets. Firstly, a piece of the CF/VMFO with a size of 3×4 cm² was placed in the center of the tube furnace and 200 mg of sodium hypophosphite (NaH2PO2) was placed upstream of the CF/VMFO. Then the furnace was heated at 280°C for 3 h at a heating rate of 2°C/min in an argon stream.

nodes.characterization_summary: VGSs show D=1334, G=1568, 2D=2680 cm⁻¹ with IG/I2D∼1.2 indicating few layers; MoS2 shows E2g¹=380.0, A1g=404.1 cm⁻¹ with 24.1 cm⁻¹ separation indicating few layers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 1334, 1568, and 2680 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to D, G, and 2D peaks of the VGSs, respectively. The ratio of IG/I2D is ∼1.2 ... The peaks ... at about 380.0 and 404.1 cm⁻¹ are E2g¹ and A1g modes of 2H-MoS2, respectively. The separation between the E2g¹ and A1g modes is 24.1 cm⁻¹, revealing few-layer feature.

There are seven diffraction peaks in the XRD pattern of the CF/VMFO. The peaks at ∼15° and 25° represent the (002) plane of 2H-MoS2 and (002) plane of graphite ... The remaining peaks correspond to the (003), (006), (012), (015), (018), and (110) crystal planes of NiFe(OH)x and NiCo(OH)x ... These peaks correspond to the (111), (201), (210), and (300) planes of Fe2P and Ni2P. Others correspond to the (011), (111), and (211) planes of CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: CF/VMFO: Fe3+ (Fe 2p3/2=712.7 eV, 2p1/2=725.0 eV), Co2+ (781.5/797.3 eV), Ni2+ (855.6/873.2 eV); CF/VMFP shows Fe2+/Fe3+, Coδ+, Co3+, Ni2P, P anions (129.3/130.1 eV) and phosphate-like P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the spectrum of Fe, the peaks at 712.7 and 725.0 eV correspond to Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 binding energies ... which is related to Fe3+. For Co, the peaks at 781.5 and 797.3 eV ... arise from Co2+. As for the spectrum of Ni, the peaks located at 855.6 and 873.2 eV ... are assigned to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 of Ni2+.

nodes.evidence_snippet: By using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICP-MS), the molar ratio of Fe, Co, and Ni in FeCoNi(OH)x has been determined to be 1:1.5:1.2 and that of Fe, Co, Ni, and P in FeCoNiPx is 1:1.4:1.1:2.6.

nodes.characterization_summary: CF/VMFO shows increased intensities at Fe, Co, Ni K-edges vs CF/VGSs/FeCoNi(OH)x indicating electron transfer from metals to O, Mo, S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with CF/VGSs/FeCoNi(OH)x, the CF/VMFO shows increased intensities at Fe, Co, and Ni K-edge XANES. This indicates the electron transfer from Fe, Co, and Ni atoms to neighboring atoms (O, Mo, and S).

nodes.characterization_summary: CF/VMFO shows symmetric ESR peaks at g=2.003 indicating oxygen vacancies in FeCoNi(OH)x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ESR spectrum of the CF/VMFO shows a pair of steep peaks with a symmetric distribution and g = 2.003, meaning electron trapping at oxygen vacancies in FeCoNi(OH)x.
